items.stem: Which F# construct is designed to make illegal states unrepresentable for a value that is exactly one of several named shapes?

options.rationale: Correct: a discriminated union lets the type hold exactly one of a fixed set of cases, so impossible combinations cannot be constructed.
A record groups several fields that all exist at once, and nullable fields reintroduce the illegal states you are trying to remove.
A string can hold any text, so the compiler cannot restrict it to the valid cases.

options.text: A mutable class with an enum flag
options.rationale: An enum plus separate fields lets invalid combinations exist and be mutated into existence.

items.explanation: Correct: a discriminated union lets the type hold exactly one of a fixed set of cases, so impossible combinations cannot be constructed.

items.stem: Which of the following are pure, immutable-by-default behaviours you can rely on in idiomatic F#? (Select TWO)

options.text: A let binding introduces an immutable value unless mark with mutable
options.rationale: Correct: let bindings are immutable by default; you must opt into mutation with mutable.

options.text: List.map returns a new list rather than modifying the input
options.rationale: Correct: the List module functions produce new collections and leave the input unchanged.

options.text: Records are reference-mutable so fields can be reassigned freely
options.rationale: Record fields are immutable by default; you create a changed copy with the with syntax.

options.text: The pipeline operator mutates its left operand in place
options.rationale: The |> operator simply passes a value as the last argument to a function; it mutates nothing.

items.explanation: Correct: let bindings are immutable by default; you must opt into mutation with mutable.; Correct: the List module functions produce new collections and leave the input unchanged.

items.stem: A validation pipeline should stop at the first failure and otherwise pass the value along. Which type best models this in F#?

options.rationale: Correct: Result carries either a success value or an error, and binding chains short-circuit on the first Error.

options.text: A thrown exception caught at the top
options.rationale: Exceptions work but are discouraged for expected validation failures because they bypass the type system and are hard to compose.

options.text: A bool returned from each step
options.rationale: A bool loses the error detail and does not carry the successful value forward.
Null cannot distinguish between the different failure reasons and reintroduces null-reference risks.

items.explanation: Correct: Result carries either a success value or an error, and binding chains short-circuit on the first Error.
